assumptions.formula: OS-positive Schwinger data reconstructs (H_YM, Omega, U(t), fields).
assumptions.name: OS/Wightman reconstruction

assumptions.formula: U(t) is strongly continuous and U(t)=e^{-itH} for a self-adjoint H.
assumptions.name: Hamiltonian generation

assumptions.formula: H >= 0, H Omega = 0, and P0 projects onto the vacuum sector.
assumptions.name: Positive energy and vacuum

assumptions.formula: Pperp H_YM != {0}; gauge-invariant observables create non-vacuum states.
assumptions.name: Nontrivial excitation sector

assumptions.formula: there exists Delta>0 such that E_H((0,Delta))Pperp = 0.
assumptions.name: Spectral lower bound

derivations.candidate_derivation: If A1-A4 construct the physical continuum theory and A5 is proved, then the target subclaim follows: Pperp H_YM is the non-vacuum sector and the spectral theorem gives inf spec(H|Pperp H_YM)>=Delta. Equivalently, H has no spectrum in (0,Delta) away from the vacuum, so the reconstructed Yang-Mills theory has a Hamiltonian mass gap.

derivation_steps.derivation: From OS/Wightman reconstruction obtain a Hilbert space H_YM, vacuum Omega, and time translations U(t). By Stone's theorem, strong continuity of U(t) yields a self-adjoint generator H with U(t)=exp(-itH).

definitions: H_YM is the Hilbert space reconstructed from OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions.
U(t) is the strongly continuous unitary group implementing real-time translations on H_YM.
H is the self-adjoint Stone generator of U(t), with positive energy imposed by the Wightman/OS target axioms.
valid_when: The Schwinger data have already passed to the continuum and satisfy OS positivity strongly enough for reconstruction.
Time translations are represented by a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group on the reconstructed Hilbert space.
The positive-energy axiom is part of the reconstructed Yang-Mills target, not borrowed from a cutoff transfer matrix alone.

derivation_steps.open_obligation: Show this H is obtained after continuum/OS reconstruction, not only at fixed lattice cutoff.
derivation_steps.title: Construct the Hamiltonian object

derivation_steps.derivation: Normalize the invariant vacuum Omega and set P0=|Omega><Omega|, or the projection onto the full vacuum sector if vacuum uniqueness is not yet known. The excitation space is Pperp H_YM=(I-P0)H_YM.

definitions: Omega is the normalized invariant vacuum vector in H_YM.
P0 is the orthogonal projection onto C Omega when the vacuum is unique; otherwise it must be replaced by the projection onto the full zero-energy vacuum sector.
Pperp is I-P0, the vacuum-orthogonal excitation projection.
valid_when: The vacuum sector has been identified inside the reconstructed continuum theory.
Either vacuum uniqueness is proved, or the formula is read with P0 as the full vacuum-sector projection.
H Omega = 0 follows from time-translation invariance of the reconstructed vacuum.

derivation_steps.open_obligation: Prove vacuum uniqueness or explicitly work with the whole zero-energy vacuum sector.
derivation_steps.title: Separate vacuum and excitations

derivation_steps.derivation: The Hamiltonian mass-gap claim is the spectral exclusion of low positive energies. In projection form, no vacuum-orthogonal state can have spectral support in (0,Delta).

definitions: E_H(B) is the spectral projection of the self-adjoint Hamiltonian H for the Borel set B.
Delta is a fixed positive number, independent of removed cutoffs, proposed as the mass-gap lower bound.
H restricted to Pperp H_YM means the part of H acting on the invariant vacuum-orthogonal excitation sector.
valid_when: Pperp commutes with H, as it does when P0 projects onto the H-invariant zero-energy vacuum sector.
The spectral theorem applies to H and the projection statement is made on the reconstructed continuum Hilbert space.
Delta is strictly positive and the interval (0, Delta) is being excluded only away from the vacuum sector.

derivation_steps.open_obligation: Derive this exclusion from constructive/RG/correlator input rather than assuming it.
derivation_steps.title: State the spectral-gap lemma

derivation_steps.derivation: By the spectral theorem, if spectral support on Pperp H_YM lies in [Delta,infty), then every vector psi in the quadratic-form domain and orthogonal to the vacuum has energy at least Delta times its norm squared.

definitions: psi is a vector in the quadratic-form domain of H and orthogonal to the vacuum sector.
mu_psi(B)=<psi,E_H(B)psi> is the spectral measure of H associated with psi.
The integral is the spectral-theorem expression for the Hamiltonian quadratic form on psi.
valid_when: The low-energy spectral exclusion E_H((0, Delta))Pperp=0 has been established.
psi lies in Pperp H_YM and in the form domain required for <psi,H psi> to be finite.
The support of mu_psi is contained in [Delta, infinity) after removal of the vacuum component.

derivation_steps.open_obligation: Identify a dense class of physical gauge-invariant excitation states to which this estimate applies.
derivation_steps.title: Convert spectral exclusion to an energy inequality

derivation_steps.derivation: For A with <Omega,A Omega>=0, the Euclidean two-point function has spectral representation. The lower spectral support gives exponential decay with rate at least Delta.

definitions: A is a reconstructed gauge-invariant observable, vacuum-subtracted so that <Omega,A Omega>=0.
C_A(t) is the Euclidean time two-point function produced by OS reconstruction.
mu_A(B)=<A Omega,E_H(B)A Omega> is the spectral measure of the excitation A Omega.
valid_when: A Omega belongs to the vacuum-orthogonal sector and to the domain needed for the Euclidean semigroup pairing.
The OS/Wightman reconstruction identifies Euclidean time translation with the semigroup exp(-tH) for t >= 0.
The spectral support of A Omega lies in [Delta, infinity), so the exponential bound follows uniformly in t >= 0.

derivation_steps.open_obligation: Specify gauge-invariant observables A and show their reconstructed states control the physical spectrum.
derivation_steps.title: Convert the same gap to Euclidean decay

derivation_steps.derivation: Conversely, exponential decay of a sufficiently rich family of vacuum-subtracted observables can imply spectral support above Delta only if the created states are dense in the excitation sector.

definitions: A_ginv is the reconstructed algebra or dense test family of gauge-invariant observables.
The bar denotes Hilbert-space closure in H_YM.
(A-<Omega,A Omega>)Omega is the vacuum-subtracted excitation created by A.
valid_when: The observable family A_ginv is part of the same reconstructed continuum Yang-Mills theory.
Gauge-invariant observables are rich enough to generate the physical vacuum-orthogonal excitation sector.
Null vectors from OS reconstruction have already been quotiented out, so closure is taken in the physical Hilbert space.

derivation_steps.open_obligation: Prove the gauge-invariant observable family is spectrally determining after reconstruction.
derivation_steps.title: Use decay-to-gap only with a density hypothesis

derivation_steps.derivation: For lattice/regulated approximants H_a, a bound inf spec(H_a|Pperp_a)>=Delta_a is useful only if liminf_{a->0}Delta_a>0 and the Hilbert spaces, observables, and vacuum sectors converge to the reconstructed continuum theory.

definitions: a is the ultraviolet cutoff or lattice spacing parameter being removed.
H_a and Pperp,a are the regulated Hamiltonian and excitation projection before continuum passage.
Delta_a is the regulated gap lower bound, and Delta is the positive lower bound surviving the limit.
valid_when: The regulated Hilbert spaces, observables, vacuum sectors, and Hamiltonians converge to the same OS-reconstructed continuum object.
The spectral or Euclidean decay estimate is uniform in the cutoff and does not deteriorate to zero as a -> 0.
The limiting excitation sector remains nontrivial and interacting, so the bound is not for an empty or Gaussian surrogate.

derivation_steps.open_obligation: Prevent the lattice gap from collapsing in the continuum limit.
derivation_steps.title: Attach continuum compatibility

derivations.mathematical_subclaim: Given a reconstructed Wightman/OS Yang-Mills theory with Hilbert space H_YM, vacuum Omega, strongly continuous time translations U(t), and Hamiltonian H satisfying U(t)=exp(-itH), prove that there is Delta>0 with spec(H restricted to Omega^perp) subset [Delta,infty).
derivations.route_text: Use a bounded Hamiltonian spectral-gap route endpoint claim only after stating which reconstructed Yang-Mills objects and observables make it meaningful: Use the Hamiltonian formulation as the endpoint check: after the physical Hilbert space, vacuum, and time-translation generator are reconstructed from the same continuum Yang-Mills data, prove that vacuum-orthogonal excitations have energy at least a strictly positive Delta.
source_obligations: Preserve the constructed Yang-Mills theory while moving to Hamiltonian spectral language.
Name the Hamiltonian, vacuum sector, and excitation subspace for the reconstructed theory.
Show the spectral gap belongs to a nontrivial interacting theory.
Explain how the Hamiltonian is obtained after continuum/OS reconstruction rather than at fixed cutoff.
Cite the mass-gap and Hamiltonian-Wightman definitions plus any transfer-matrix evidence.
Split into Hilbert-space construction, vacuum uniqueness/isolation, excitation spectrum, and positive lower-bound sublemmas.
Hamiltonian construction lemma: define H as the time-translation generator of the reconstructed theory.
Vacuum isolation lemma: identify the vacuum and prove it is separated from non-vacuum states.
Spectral lower-bound lemma: prove inf spec(H on vacuum-orthogonal sector) >= Delta for some Delta > 0.
Continuum compatibility lemma: show the spectral bound survives the limiting construction.
derivations.source_witness: Systematically navigate the Yang-Mills existence and mass gap proof-discovery space while preserving the essential Clay target commitments over long-horizon hypothesis exploration.

symbols.E_H(B): spectral projection of H for Borel set B
symbols.H: positive self-adjoint Hamiltonian, the generator of U(t)
symbols.H_YM: physical Hilbert space produced by OS/Wightman reconstruction
symbols.Omega: vacuum vector, normalized and invariant under time translations
symbols.P0: orthogonal projection onto the vacuum sector C Omega
symbols.Pperp: I-P0, the projection onto the vacuum-orthogonal excitation sector

what_does_not_count: A spectral gap for a fixed lattice spacing without continuum stability.
A heuristic or numerical lower bound not expressed as a spectral theorem statement.
A Hamiltonian defined before OS/Wightman reconstruction of the continuum target.
Decay of observables that do not determine the vacuum-orthogonal spectrum.

what_would_count_as_progress.claim: A precise construction of H_YM, Omega, U(t), and H from OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions.
what_would_count_as_progress.why: This is the mathematical bridge from Euclidean functional data to the Hamiltonian problem. Without reconstructed objects H_YM, Omega, U(t), and a self-adjoint generator H, the phrase 'spectral gap' is only a desired notation, not a claim about the target continuum Yang-Mills theory.

what_would_count_as_progress.claim: A proof that gauge-invariant observables create a dense excitation sector.
what_would_count_as_progress.why: A gap detected by a narrow observable family could miss hidden low-energy states. Density is what lets decay estimates or spectral bounds for gauge-invariant observables control the whole vacuum-orthogonal physical sector P_perp H_YM.

what_would_count_as_progress.claim: A cutoff-uniform lower spectral bound or equivalent cutoff-uniform Euclidean decay estimate.
what_would_count_as_progress.why: The Clay target is a continuum problem, so a fixed-regulator lattice gap is not enough: it can collapse when the cutoff is removed. Uniformity is the mechanism that transfers a regulated spectral or decay estimate into a positive lower bound for the reconstructed continuum Hamiltonian.

what_would_count_as_progress.claim: A nontriviality witness showing the excitation sector belongs to an interacting Yang-Mills theory.
what_would_count_as_progress.why: The mass-gap statement must be about the nontrivial interacting gauge theory, not a free, Gaussian, empty, or mismatched limit. A nontriviality witness ties the excitation sector carrying the gap to the same continuum Yang-Mills object produced by the construction.

scope: This derives the exact spectral subclaim that the Hamiltonian route must prove. It does not prove Yang-Mills; it exposes the mathematical load-bearing lemmas and the spectral-theorem consequences.
